item.title: Colombia's James Rodriguez retires from international football
item.description: Colombia midfielder James Rodriguez retired from international football on Tuesday, having won 131 caps and inspired his country to the 2014 World Cup quarter-finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombia midfielder James Rodriguez retired from international football on Tuesday, having won 131 caps and inspired his country to the 2014 World Cup quarter-finals. "Thank you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the greatest honours of my life," Rodriguez said in a video posted on social media. The 35-year-old, who made his senior debut in 2011 and often captained Colombia, scored 31 goals and represented his country at three World Cups and four Copa America tournaments. Rodriguez rose to global prominence at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, scoring six goals to win the Golden Boot as Colombia reached the quarter-finals. His volley against Uruguay in the last 16 earned him FIFA’s Puskas Award for the best goal of the year. He signed for Colombian side Atletico Nacional last week on a deal running until next June after leaving Major League Soccer club Minnesota United. Rodriguez previously played for Real Madrid, winning two Champions League and two LaLiga titles, and also had spells with Bayern Munich and Everton.

item.title: Attorney General Blanche says FBI has new information on man who shot Trump
item.description: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday that the FBI had discovered new information regarding the shooter who attempted to assassinate Donald Trump during a campaign event in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024.
item.dc:creator: Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff, Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday that the FBI had discovered new information regarding the shooter who attempted to assassinate Donald Trump during a campaign event in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024. "It is new information about the shooter and about his background, about his history and that stuff that we didn't know before," Blanche told reporters during a White House press conference, without elaborating. The comments from Blanche came hours after Trump claimed on social media that new information was found about the assassination attempt and alleged without evidence that it was really a "Democrat Plot, to get me out of the Election." Investigations into the shooting have found the shooter acted alone and produced no evidence Democrats had anything to do with the shooting. Trump added that ex-FBI Director Christopher Wray, whom Trump appointed in his first term but later grew to hate, "should pay a price" for how the department responded to the assassination attempt "and certainly for the things he said." Blanche, who was Trump's personal lawyer at the time of the assassination attempt, said during the briefing that he was with Trump as the investigation into the shooting was playing out, trying to ascertain what happened. "His frustration and concern about what the former director was doing is something that is not new," Blanche said. The Justice Department and FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Wray could not be reached for comment.

item.title: Syngenta entra com pedido de IPO para levantar ao menos US$5 bi, dizem fontes
item.description: A Syngenta Group, empresa suíça do setor de sementes e agroquímicos, apresentou confidencialmente um pedido de oferta pública inicial (IPO) em Hong Kong, com o objetivo de levantar pelo menos US$ 5 bilhões, segundo três pessoas com conhecimento direto do assunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Syngenta Group, empresa suíça do setor de sementes e agroquímicos, apresentou confidencialmente um pedido de oferta pública inicial (IPO) em Hong Kong, com o objetivo de levantar pelo menos US$ 5 bilhões, segundo três pessoas com conhecimento direto do assunto. A empresa sediada em Basileia, controlada pela estatal chinesa Sinochem (600500.SS) , espera lançar a oferta ainda no final deste ano ou, caso contrário, no início de 2027, afirmaram duas das fontes. Dependendo da resposta do mercado, o tamanho da oferta poderia chegar a US$10 bilhões, disseram as fontes. Com esse valor, seria a maior oferta pública inicial de Hong Kong desde 2010, segundo dados da LSEG. O mercado de IPOs de Hong Kong está em franca expansão, com ofertas públicas iniciais e listagens secundárias arrecadando US$45,8 bilhões até agora neste ano, em comparação com US$24 bilhões no mesmo período do ano passado, segundo dados da LSEG. O prazo exato, o tamanho da oferta e a avaliação da empresa ainda não foram definidos, afirmaram as fontes, que preferiram não se identificar, já que a informação não é de domínio público. Uma listagem desse porte testaria o apetite dos investidores por uma empresa cuja proprietária, a Sinochem, pagou US$43 bilhões para torná-la privada em 2017 e ainda não conseguiu alinhar esse investimento a uma avaliação do mercado público. O sucesso proporcionaria a Hong Kong uma de suas principais transações do ano e daria à Syngenta uma maneira de começar a quitar parte de suas dívidas, além de investir em novos produtos de proteção de culturas e sementes. A Syngenta espera que o mercado agrícola global melhore no próximo ano, especialmente se houver uma resolução no conflito com o Irã que alivie a escassez de gás natural usado na fabricação de fertilizantes, tornando os produtos mais baratos para os agricultores, disse uma pessoa a par do assunto. A empresa também quer aproveitar ao máximo o mercado de ações em alta de Hong Kong antes que ele esfrie, acrescentou a fonte, enquanto o recém-nomeado presidente-executivo Hengde Qin, de nacionalidade chinesa, é visto como alguém capaz de conduzir os diversos processos de aprovação. "Não comentamos especulações de mercado", afirmou a Syngenta em resposta à Reuters. A Sinochem não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. A Bloomberg News foi a primeira a noticiar o pedido na terça-feira, informando que a empresa está considerando levantar cerca de US$5 bilhões. (Reportagem de Bipasha Dey em Bengaluru, Yantoultra Ngui e Kane Wu em Hong Kong e John Revill em Zurique)

item.title: 3M, DuPont must face Connecticut firefighters' lawsuit over 'forever chemicals'
item.description: A federal judge on Tuesday said more than 20 defendants including 3M , DuPont and Honeywell must face claims by Connecticut firefighters who said their protective gear was contaminated by toxic "forever chemicals" that increased their risk of cancer.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Tuesday said more than 20 defendants including 3M (MMM.N) , DuPont (DD.N) and Honeywell (HON.O) must face claims by Connecticut firefighters who said their protective gear was contaminated by toxic "forever chemicals" that increased their risk of cancer. Lawyers for 13 firefighter union organizations and 12 individual firefighters said "turnout gear" that shields against extreme heat and flames leached the chemicals through absorption into skin, ingestion and inhalation. They have [USN:L1N3IN10I TEXT:"called the proposed class action"] the first to exclusively target firefighter gear containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS. U.S. District Judge Alvin Thompson in Hartford, Connecticut, said the unions had "organizational" standing to seek damages, and firefighters could seek damages and medical monitoring even if they had no outward symptoms of cancer and other diseases. The judge also said the plaintiffs sufficiently alleged that 3M, one of the largest manufacturers of PFAS, owed a duty to warn about the risks and committed negligence. PFAS in firefighters' protective gear included 3M's Scotchlite reflective material and DuPont's Kevlar, while Honeywell manufactured turnout gear, according to the complaint. Some DuPont liabilities now belong to two spinoffs, Chemours (CC.N) and Corteva (CTVA.N) . Lawyers for 3M, DuPont, Chemours, Corteva and Honeywell did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Jennifer Sclar, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said the decision was significant because it found that prolonged exposure to PFAS from turnout gear justified legal standing. PFAS WIDELY USED In seeking dismissals, 3M said there were no plausible claims tying Scotchlite to firefighters' gear, while other defendants said there was no allegation that the gear "failed to serve its function of protecting firefighters from the hazards of fighting fires." The lawsuit began in June 2024. PFAS are found in hundreds of consumer and commercial products including cosmetics, non-stick pans and stain-resistant clothing. They are known as "forever chemicals" because they do not break down easily in the human body or environment. PFAS have also been linked to higher cholesterol, low birth weight and reduced antibody response to vaccines. In 2023, DuPont, 3M and two other companies reached more than $11 billion in settlements to resolve claims that firefighting foam and other products containing their PFAS polluted drinking water. None admitted wrongdoing.

item.title: Volante y capitán James Rodríguez deja la selección colombiana de fútbol
item.description: El volante James Rodríguez anunció el martes su retiro de la selección colombiana de fútbol después de 15 años de vestir la camiseta del equipo nacional con el que jugó 131 partidos y participó en tres Mundiales y cuatro Copas América.
item.dc:creator: Luis Jaime Acosta
item.content:encoded: El volante James Rodríguez anunció el martes su retiro de la selección colombiana de fútbol después de 15 años de vestir la camiseta del equipo nacional con el que jugó 131 partidos y participó en tres Mundiales y cuatro Copas América. Rodríguez, de 35 años y quien era el capitán de la selección colombiana, dio a conocer su decisión cinco días después de anunciar su vinculación contractual con el club Atlético Nacional de Medellín. "Llegó el momento. Gracias por cada partido, cada alegría, cada lágrima y cada sueño compartido", dijo el deportista en una publicación en sus redes sociales. "Defender los colores de la selección Colombia fue uno de los mayores honores de mi vida. Gracias, Colombia. Para siempre", aseguró. James Rodríguez nació en Cúcuta, debutó en el Envigado y luego dio el salto internacional con Banfield de Argentina, donde fue el jugador extranjero más joven en debutar, marcar y ganar un título en la liga. Pasó al Porto de Portugal, donde ganó seis títulos y el Balón de Oro portugués, y en 2013 fichó por el Mónaco de Francia por una cifra histórica del club en ese momento. Su gran actuación en el Mundial de Brasil 2014, donde ganó la Bota de Oro y el Premio Puskás por su gol ante Uruguay, lo llevó al Real Madrid, club en el que ganó dos Ligas y dos Champions League. Luego jugó cedido en el Bayern Múnich, y posteriormente tuvo pasos por Everton, Al-Rayyan, Olympiacos, São Paulo, Rayo Vallecano, León y Minnesota United. "Tuve el honor de llevar la camiseta número 10 y también la cinta de capitán. Siempre intenté hacerlo con respeto, con responsabilidad y entendiendo lo que significaba representar a Colombia. Hubo días buenos y otros muy difíciles, pero nunca dejé de sentir orgullo por esos colores", afirmó el deportista. "Sé que vienen nuevas generaciones, nuevos jugadores, nuevos sueños. A ellos les deseo lo mejor, que entiendan siempre el privilegio que significa vestir esa camiseta y que la defiendan con el alma. Yo me voy tranquilo porque sé que lo di absolutamente todo", concluyó Rodríguez al agradecer a Colombia por su apoyo. Varios jugadores de la selección colombiana reaccionaron en sus redes sociales a la salida de Rodríguez del equipo cafetero. "Gracias por hacernos crecer y dejar el nombre de nuestro país en alto. Gracias leyenda", dijo el delantero Luis Suárez. "Épico y diferente entre todos, siempre MI CAPITÁN", sostuvo por su parte el mediocampista Jefferson Lerma.

item.title: US Congress Democrats probe Russian oligarch financing of Trump Jr. wedding parties
item.description: Democrats in the U.S. Congress launched an investigation this week into reports that a Russian oligarch paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the wedding celebrations of President Donald Trump's son earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Richard Cowan, Alexandra Ulmer
item.content:encoded: Democrats in the U.S. Congress launched an investigation this week into reports that a Russian oligarch paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the wedding celebrations of President Donald Trump's son earlier this year. The Democrats' move comes on the heels of an article by ProPublica that Umar Kremlev, a wealthy Russian businessman and president of the International Boxing Association, paid for wedding festivities for Donald Trump Jr. in the Bahamas in May. The report said that Kremlev has close ties to the Russian government. "Why is a Russian oligarch and friend of Vladimir Putin financially supporting the President's son? What does Umar Kremlev expect in return for funding this three-day wedding in the Bahamas?" Representative Robert Garcia wrote on Tuesday in a social media post. Garcia is the senior Democrat on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and is expected to chair the panel if Democrats win a majority in the House of Representatives in November's midterm elections. A representative for Don Jr declined to comment. His wife, Bettina Trump, said in an Instagram post on Monday that Kremlev was a friend who had extended an "extraordinarily generous wedding gift," stressing that Kremlev had paid for two after-parties, not the wedding itself. Kremlev and the IBA did not respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. The president, who did not attend his son's wedding, said in a statement that he did not know Kremlev and that the wedding controversy was "not a big deal!" Aides to Republican Representative James Comer of Kentucky, who chairs the committee, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Garcia and other leading House Democrats already have been gearing up for probes into Trump, his family and ethics questions that have arisen since the start of the president's second term in January 2025. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer of New York on Tuesday called the wedding arrangement "so corrupt, so venal, so endangering our national security." In a speech to the Senate, Schumer added, "You’re dealing with a Russian oligarch, not just a cousin who’s giving you a gift...sometimes a wedding gift is a bribe from a foreign autocrat."

item.title: Sanders e Bannon pedem restrições à IA em meio à inquietação popular
item.description: Bernie Sanders, senador progressista norte-americano, e Steve Bannon, um aliado próximo do presidente Donald Trump, pediram nesta terça-feira que sejam impostas restrições aos sistemas de IA, unindo dois adversários políticos em torno da preocupação de que a tecnologia possa prejudicar os seres humanos.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: Bernie Sanders, senador progressista norte-americano, e Steve Bannon, um aliado próximo do presidente Donald Trump, pediram nesta terça-feira que sejam impostas restrições aos sistemas de IA, unindo dois adversários políticos em torno da preocupação de que a tecnologia possa prejudicar os seres humanos. Os dois deveriam participar do mesmo encontro em Washington, em meio à crescente preocupação popular com os riscos da IA para além de Washington e do Vale do Silício. Primeiro a se manifestar, Sanders, que se autodenomina socialista democrático, alertou sobre a “ameaça crescente” da IA e afirmou que o setor precisa ser regulamentado com normas de segurança vinculativas. “A IA tem o potencial de eliminar dezenas de milhões de empregos, acabando com profissões inteiras e tornando mais difícil para nossos jovens ingressarem no mercado de trabalho.” E acrescentou: “Como muitos cientistas acreditam que possa acontecer, essa tecnologia escapará ao controle humano, com consequências potencialmente catastróficas.” Sanders recebeu aplausos da plateia ao criticar executivos do setor de tecnologia por centralizarem o controle sobre a tecnologia de IA, incluindo o presidente-executivo da SpaceX e ex-assessor de Trump, Elon Musk. “No mês passado, ficamos sabendo que a IA foi usada pela primeira vez na história para criar novos vírus. Nas mãos erradas, isso poderia levar ao surgimento de novas armas biológicas e a uma possível pandemia global que poderia causar a morte de dezenas de milhões de pessoas”, disse Sanders. Bannon, ex-estrategista da Casa Branca durante o primeiro mandato presidencial de Trump, criticou a abordagem de Trump em relação à supervisão da IA, atribuindo diretamente às empresas de tecnologia a culpa pela relutância do presidente em regulamentar a tecnologia. Em seu podcast de segunda-feira, Bannon disse que o Congresso não deveria aprovar leis que proíbam os Estados de aplicar suas próprias regras para a tecnologia. ALIADOS IMPROVÁVEIS A decisão de Sanders e Bannon, que estão em extremos opostos do espectro ideológico dos Estados Unidos, de discursarem no mesmo evento nesta terça-feira ressalta como as preocupações com a IA e os data centers ultrapassam as divisões partidárias e geram alianças políticas improváveis. Na segunda-feira, Trump minimizou preocupações expressas por líderes do setor no fim de semana sobre o uso indevido da inteligência artificial, afirmando que os EUA já contam com medidas de proteção para a poderosa tecnologia. Apoiando a posição de Trump nesta terça-feira, o presidente republicano da Câmara dos Deputados dos EUA, Mike Johnson, disse que não pode haver uma moratória no desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial sem perder a vantagem competitiva para a China e que as empresas de IA podem se autorregular. “Elas podem se autorregular. Não precisam que o governo lhes diga para desacelerar. Se quiserem desacelerar, que o façam”, disse Johnson a jornalistas. A visão de que as regulamentações prejudicarão a capacidade das empresas norte-americanas de competir com suas contrapartes chinesas é compartilhada por executivos do setor de tecnologia, incluindo Jensen Huang, presidente-executivo da Nvidia (NVDA.O) . Pesquisas recentes revelaram que a maioria dos norte-americanos teme que a tecnologia possa ser usada para eliminar empregos, aumentar os custos para as famílias ou causar outros danos sociais. O pesquisador da Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, chamou a atenção do público na semana passada ao afirmar que se demitiu da empresa, em parte porque “as pessoas que desenvolvem IA acreditam sinceramente que ela pode nos matar a todos até o final da década”. Também nesta terça-feira, Andrew Ferguson, presidente da Comissão Federal de Comércio dos EUA, expressou suspeitas sobre empresas de IA que buscam isenções antitruste enquanto, ao mesmo tempo, fazem lobby por novas regulamentações. A Reuters havia noticiado anteriormente que senadores dos EUA estão debatendo um projeto de lei que impediria Estados de aplicar suas próprias leis para regulamentar certos riscos apresentados por modelos de IA. Tentativas anteriores de restringir leis estaduais sobre IA fracassaram no Senado dos EUA.

item.title: Renault, Geely to invest €319 million in Brazil, expand partnership
item.description: Automakers Renault and Geely said on Tuesday they will make a new €319 million investment in Brazil, through their joint venture, reinforcing their industrial partnership in the largest Latin American market, where rival BYD has been gaining ground with its affordable pure electric and plug-in hybrid models.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Automakers Renault (RENA.PA) and Geely (0175.HK) said on Tuesday they will make a new €319 million investment in Brazil, through their joint venture, reinforcing their industrial partnership in the largest Latin American market, where rival BYD (002594.SZ) has been gaining ground with its affordable pure electric and plug-in hybrid models. Renault [USN:L8N3WU1CD TEXT:"announced last fall"] the completion of a deal in Brazil with Geely. The new investment brings the companies' total investments in Brazil to €899 million between 2025 and 2027. The agreement allows Geely access to an existing plant and dealership network and will help the French carmaker to use more of the available capacity at its assembly plant and add larger models to its portfolio, Renault has said. Renault said its Hybrid E-Tech 4x4 flex-fuel technology will enter production in Brazil in 2027 under a new investment plan.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A exportação de soja do Brasil foi estimada nesta terça-feira em 8,32 milhões de toneladas, aumento de mais de 500 mil toneladas no comparativo com a semana anterior, de acordo com projeções semanais da Associação Nacional dos Exportadores de Cereais (Anec). item.title: Accionistas de grupo energético colombiano Ecopetrol aprueban nueva junta directiva
item.description: Los accionistas del grupo energético colombiano Ecopetrol aprobaron el martes los nuevos nombramientos de la junta directiva del conglomerado, propuestos por el Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los accionistas del grupo energético colombiano Ecopetrol aprobaron el martes los nuevos nombramientos de la junta directiva del conglomerado, propuestos por el Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella. Dentro del directorio de nueve miembros fueron ratificados Luis Felipe Henao, César Loza y Ricardo Rodríguez Yee. Los seis nuevos integrantes de la junta son Carlos Augusto Suárez, José Camilo Manzur Jattin, Jorge Alberto Jaller Jaramillo, Ludmila del Carmen Vergara, Betzy Patricia Martínez y Claudia Margarita Lafaurie Taboada. El lunes por la noche, el presidente encargado de la compañía, Juan Carlos Hurtado, se retiró por mutuo acuerdo y será reemplazado temporalmente por el actual vicepresidente corporativo de finanzas, Camilo Barco. Medios locales dijeron que la dimisión de Hurtado estuvo relacionada con supuestas irregularidades en negocios y nombramientos de personal. Ecopetrol no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters. Hurtado, quien previamente ostentaba el cargo de vicepresidente ejecutivo de hidrocarburos, había asumido por primera vez como presidente encargado en abril, y de nuevo de forma definitiva desde el 31 de julio, en reemplazo de Ricardo Roa, quien se apartó de la presidencia en medio de acusaciones de tráfico de influencias y de violación de los límites de gastos de la campaña del expresidente Gustavo Petro en 2022. Los mercados se mantienen a la expectativa de que el Gobierno anuncie el nuevo presidente de Ecopetrol. El Estado es el principal accionista de Ecopetrol, con una participación del 88,49% en la empresa más importante del país. La empresa genera la mayor parte de la producción de petróleo a nivel nacional y es propietaria de las dos principales refinerías y de la mayor parte de la red de oleoductos y poliductos. Docenas de funcionarios de Ecopetrol han renunciado o han sido despedidos tras la posesión de De La Espriella. Ecopetrol ha estado inmersa en varios escándalos por supuesta corrupción y tráfico de influencias de algunos funcionarios nombrados durante el Gobierno del expresidente Petro, que, aunque son investigados por las autoridades, aún no han sido condenados.

item.title: Ecopetrol approves government-backed board overhaul
item.description: Colombia's state-controlled oil company Ecopetrol on Tuesday approved a sweeping board overhaul proposed by newly inaugurated President Abelardo De La Espriella's government, as the company reels from corruption allegations and another senior management shake-up.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombia's state-controlled oil company Ecopetrol on Tuesday approved a sweeping board overhaul proposed by newly inaugurated President Abelardo De La Espriella's government, as the company reels from corruption allegations and another senior management shake-up. Current chairman Luis Felipe Henao was reappointed to the nine-member board, along with Cesar Loza, and Ricardo Rodriguez Yee. Whether Henao will continue as chair will be decided by the new board in an upcoming meeting. The revamp comes a day after Ecopetrol announced that acting CEO Juan Carlos Hurtado would leave by mutual agreement, effective Tuesday, extending a period of turmoil at Colombia's most important company. Ecopetrol said late on Monday that Camilo Barco, its finance chief, would take over on an interim basis. Local media linked Hurtado's exit to alleged irregularities in contracting and appointments. Ecopetrol did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the move. Hurtado, previously head of hydrocarbons, had led the company on an interim basis since April, when Ricardo Roa stepped down over accusations of influence peddling and campaign finance violations tied to former President Gustavo Petro's 2022 election campaign. Markets are now awaiting the government's choice for a new CEO. The Colombian government owns 88.49% of Ecopetrol, the country's biggest oil producer. The company also operates Colombia's two main refineries and most of its oil and fuel pipeline network. Dozens of Ecopetrol officials have resigned or been dismissed since De La Espriella took office in early August. Ecopetrol has been hit by a series of scandals involving alleged corruption and influence peddling by officials appointed during Petro's government. Those under investigation have not been convicted.

item.title: Report: Dolphins S Kyle Louis sidelined by MCL sprain
item.description: Miami Dolphins rookie safety Kyle Louis sustained an MCL sprain in his NFL debut Sunday and is expected to miss a few weeks, NFL Network reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Miami Dolphins rookie safety Kyle Louis sustained an MCL sprain in his NFL debut Sunday and is expected to miss a few weeks, NFL Network reported on Tuesday. Head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters Monday night that Louis will miss at least the Week 2 game at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday but said he did not know the full extent of the knee injury. Louis, 22, is listed as a second-string safety on the depth chart. He was hurt in Miami's 27-13 road loss to the Las Vegas Raiders to open the season. He played three snaps on defense and 14 on special teams. Miami selected Louis in the fourth round out of Pittsburgh, where he played linebacker from 2022-25. --Field Level Media

item.title: US attorney general says probes handled by ex-prosecutor DiGenova will continue
item.description: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday that any probes that former federal prosecutor Joseph DiGenova had been handling would continue.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday that any probes that former federal prosecutor Joseph DiGenova had been handling would continue. DiGenova, who oversaw a wide-ranging probe into past investigations of President Donald Trump, [USN:L6N4521BD TEXT:"resigned"] last week. "I very much appreciate the work that he did for us and for the administration," Blanche told reporters at the White house. "Any investigations that he's working on, of course, continue like they do, like any investigation does when somebody leaves, and we're not going to slow down just because somebody leaves." DiGenova joined the Justice Department in April to take over the Florida-based investigation that has been scrutinizing several of Trump’s foes and has sought to establish that the president was the victim of a long-running criminal conspiracy. The investigation has examined the 2017 U.S. intelligence finding that Russia sought to boost Trump’s first presidential campaign in 2016, as well as more recent investigations by former Special Counsel Jack Smith that probed Trump’s retention of classified documents at his Mar-a-Lago resort and his attempts to overturn his 2020 election defeat. The investigation has so far not resulted in any criminal charges. DiGenova, a Trump ally, did not provide a reason for his resignation.

item.title: Alex Saab, aliado de Maduro, se declara culpado em processo de corrupção nos EUA
item.description: Um empresário nascido na Colômbia, com laços estreitos com o presidente venezuelano deposto Nicolás Maduro, se declarou culpado nesta terça-feira em um processo de corrupção nos Estados Unidos, enquanto promotores federais se preparam, em um processo separado, para levar Maduro a julgamento no próximo ano.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen, Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: Um empresário nascido na Colômbia, com laços estreitos com o presidente venezuelano deposto Nicolás Maduro, se declarou culpado nesta terça-feira em um processo de corrupção nos Estados Unidos, enquanto promotores federais se preparam, em um processo separado, para levar Maduro a julgamento no próximo ano. Alex Saab se declarou culpado de uma acusação de conspiração para lavagem de dinheiro em uma audiência perante a juíza federal Kathleen Williams, em Miami, segundo registros do tribunal. Ele também concordou em abrir mão de US$195 milhões e cooperar com o Departamento de Justiça dos EUA. Os autos do processo não revelaram a natureza das investigações nas quais Saab poderia oferecer ajuda. Os advogados de Saab não responderam imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Os promotores afirmaram que Saab roubou milhões de dólares de um programa de assistência social destinado a ajudar a alimentar venezuelanos carentes e transferiu parte dos recursos para contas bancárias nos EUA. Ele havia se declarado inocente em julho, dois meses após ser extraditado como parte da tentativa da presidente interina da Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, de se desvincular de partes do governo de seu antecessor. Saab atuou no governo de Maduro como ministro da Indústria da Venezuela, antes de ser destituído por Rodríguez em janeiro, logo após a captura de Maduro pelas Forças Especiais dos EUA em Caracas. O novo governo da Venezuela deteve Saab no mês seguinte. O processo criminal nos EUA é o segundo contra Saab. Em 2020, ele foi detido em Cabo Verde e extraditado no ano seguinte para responder a acusações de lavagem de dinheiro por supostamente ter desviado US$350 milhões da Venezuela em conexão com um esquema de suborno. O então presidente dos EUA, Joe Biden, concedeu clemência a Saab em dezembro de 2023, como parte de uma troca de prisioneiros. Maduro está detido sem fiança em uma prisão do Brooklyn, após se declarar inocente das acusações de tráfico de drogas. Ele alega imunidade contra processos nos EUA por ter liderado um país soberano. Especialistas jurídicos consideram essa uma batalha difícil, em parte porque Washington não reconhece Maduro como presidente da Venezuela desde 2019. O julgamento de Maduro está marcado para 1º de junho de 2027.

item.title: No hay registro de que Brasil decretara que ciudadanos argentinos “no son bienvenidos”
item.description: No hay evidencia de que el Gobierno brasileño haya decretado que los ciudadanos argentinos “no son bienvenidos” u ordenado “sacar a los argentinos del país”, contrario a lo que señalan publicaciones en redes sociales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: No hay evidencia de que el Gobierno brasileño haya decretado que los ciudadanos argentinos “no son bienvenidos” u ordenado “sacar a los argentinos del país”, contrario a lo que señalan publicaciones en redes sociales. Ejemplos en Facebook dicen: “En una orden presidencial, acaban de decretar que los argentinos no son bienvenidos a Brasil, un acto de hermandad hacia México”. Las relaciones diplomáticas entre ambos países se tensaron tras los [USN:L1N43S03E TEXT:"ataques"] verbales del presidente Javier Milei contra Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y permanecen deterioradas luego de que Brasil [USN:S0N43402M TEXT:"retiró"] a su embajador en Buenos Aires. Sin embargo, no hay registro de que el Gobierno brasileño haya anunciado una restricción de viajes o expulsión de ciudadanos argentinos. La Secretaría de Comunicación Social de la Presidencia de Brasil dijo a Reuters en un correo el 14 de septiembre que las publicaciones en redes sociales son falsas. “No hubo ninguna medida en ese sentido, como tampoco existe ninguna propuesta con ese alcance en discusión”, agregó. Mariana Marshall, portavoz de la embajada de Brasil en Buenos Aires, dijo a Reuters en un correo el 10 de septiembre que no existe “la posibilidad legal, en Brasil, de que el Poder Público tome una medida para establecer que la población entera de un país no es bienvenida”. No hay reportes creíbles en medios de comunicación de que esta sea una medida o decreto presidencial de Brasil. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Brasil dice que los ciudadanos argentinos están exentos de solicitar una visa de turismo y negocios (también conocida como VIVIS ) para entrar al país por un periodo hasta de 90 días. La institución homónima en Argentina dice que, como parte de las naciones del Mercosur, para entrar a Brasil se necesita una identificación y el pasaporte. Los ministerios de relaciones exteriores de Argentina y de Brasil no respondieron a una solicitud de comentarios. VEREDICTO Sin evidencia. No hay registro de que Brasil decretara que los ciudadanos argentinos “no son bienvenidos” en el país. Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos. Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

item.title: GRANOS Soja sube tras los datos de la molienda en EEUU y el trigo se recupera
item.description: Los futuros de la soja estadounidense subían el martes, ya que los de la harina de soja se dispararon un 2% después de que un informe mensual del sector reveló que el ritmo de molienda de la oleaginosa en agosto fue inferior al esperado, dijeron analistas.
item.dc:creator: Julie Ingwersen
item.content:encoded: Los futuros de la soja estadounidense subían el martes, ya que los de la harina de soja se dispararon un 2% después de que un informe mensual del sector reveló que el ritmo de molienda de la oleaginosa en agosto fue inferior al esperado, dijeron analistas. El repunte de los precios del petróleo crudo supuso más apoyo para la soja y el maíz, que se usan en la producción de biocombustibles. Los futuros del trigo también subieron. A las 1805 GMT, los futuros de soja para noviembre de la Bolsa de Chicago ganaban 13 centavos, o un 1%, a 13,1725 dólares por bushel, y los futuros de la harina de soja para diciembre , los más activos, subían 8,50 dólares, o un 2,4%, a 364,70 dólares por tonelada. El maíz para diciembre subía 2 centavos, a 5,3525 dólares por bushel, y el trigo para el mismo mes ganaba 6,5 centavos, a 7,285 dólares por bushel. Los futuros de la soja y la harina de soja alcanzaron máximos de sesión después de que la Asociación Nacional de Procesadores de Semillas Oleaginosas (NOPA) anunció que sus miembros procesaron 205,456 millones de bushels de soja en agosto, un mínimo de 11 meses, y que las existencias de aceite de soja cayeron a mínimos desde noviembre de 2024. Los futuros del aceite de soja recortaron pérdidas y repuntaron tras la publicación del informe. "El sector de los aceites comestibles en general sigue viéndose respaldado por la creciente demanda mundial de biocombustibles en medio de la actual crisis energética provocada por las perturbaciones tanto en Oriente Medio como en el mar Negro", señaló Mike Castle, economista especializado en materias primas de StoneX, en una nota a sus clientes. Los futuros del trigo subieron al desvanecerse las esperanzas de una distensión militar en el mar Negro, tras nuevos ataques contra infraestructuras. Los precios habían caído el día anterior tras el anuncio del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de que Ucrania y Rusia habían acordado detener los ataques. "Hasta ahora, este acuerdo entre Ucrania y Rusia no pasa de ser palabrería", dijo Tom Fritz, socio de EFG Group en Chicago.

item.title: White Sox bring up LHP Noah Schultz, DFA RHP Jose Urquidy
item.description: The Chicago White Sox recalled rookie left-hander Noah Schultz from Triple-A Charlotte on Tuesday and designated veteran right-hander Jose Urquidy for assignment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Chicago White Sox recalled rookie left-hander Noah Schultz from Triple-A Charlotte on Tuesday and designated veteran right-hander Jose Urquidy for assignment. Schultz, 23, is 3-9 with a 6.06 ERA in 15 games (14 starts) since making his debut on April 14. The 2022 first-round draft pick is 3-2 with a 2.01 ERA in 11 games (10 starts) with Charlotte. Urquidy, 31, last pitched on Sept. 8 when he allowed two runs on five hits in four innings in a 9-3 home loss to the Pittsburgh Pirates. The native of Mexico went 2-1 with a 4.37 ERA in six games (one start) for the White Sox, who acquired him on July 26 from the Pirates for minor league right-hander Felix Doroteo. For his career, Urquidy is 29-18 with two saves and a 4.08 ERA over 92 games (71 starts) for the Houston Astros (2019-23), Detroit Tigers (2025), Pirates (2026) and White Sox. Chicago also activated rookie right-hander Tyler Davis from the bereavement list and optioned him to Charlotte. --Field Level Media

item.title: On verge of camp, Red Wings name Shawn Horcoff interim GM
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings announced Monday that former NHL player Shawn Horcoff will serve as interim general manager.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings announced Monday that former NHL player Shawn Horcoff will serve as interim general manager. Horcoff joined the Red Wings' front office in 2016 upon his retirement and most recently served as assistant general manager. Prior to his 2022 promotion, he also worked as director of player development, assistant director of player personnel, and GM of the Grand Rapids Griffins of the American Hockey League. The Red Wings open training camp on Thursday, which is Horcoff's 48th birthday. They open the season at home on Oct. 2 against the New York Rangers. Horcoff takes over for Steve Yzerman, a Hockey Hall of Fame member who played 22 seasons for the Red Wings. After retirement, Yzerman went to work in the Detroit front office, then became the general manager of the Tampa Bay Lightning. He returned to Detroit as GM after the 2018-19 season. He stepped down after the 2025-26 season, with the team failing to make the Stanley Cup playoffs on his watch, and is staying with the organization as a senior adviser. Horcoff will report to Red Wings governor and CEO Chris Ilitch. Horcoff will manage day-to-day roster decisions, the salary cap and hockey operations personnel. "I'm appreciative of Shawn for stepping up to serve in this capacity," Ilitch said. "His knowledge of our organization and range of experience allows us to operate with a clear decision-maker in place for the season ahead, while maintaining our commitment to carry out a thorough, methodical search process on our own timeline. Shawn has my complete support, and the authority to make decisions in the best interests of our organization. "Our search has attracted significant interest in the head of hockey operations position from respected leaders across the industry, and several of those candidates, including Shawn, remain under consideration for the permanent role." A fourth-round pick by Edmonton in the 1998 NHL Draft, Horcoff played in 1,008 games with the Oilers (2000-13), Dallas Stars (2013-15) and Anaheim Ducks (2015-16). A center, he scored 511 career points (186 goals, 325 assists). --Field Level Media

item.title: Some physical oil cargoes top $130 a barrel, nearing April's record, on Saudi disruptions
item.description: Prices for some physical oil cargoes in Europe have jumped to more than $130 a barrel on Tuesday, approaching record highs reached in April, as buyers rush to find alternatives to Middle East supplies facing increasing disruptions from intensifying conflict in the region.
item.dc:creator: Robert Harvey
item.content:encoded: Prices for some physical oil cargoes in Europe have jumped to more than $130 a barrel on Tuesday, approaching record highs reached in April, as buyers rush to find alternatives to Middle East supplies facing increasing disruptions from intensifying conflict in the region. Adding to disruptions linked to the Iran war, Saudi Arabia has cancelled late-September cargoes to European buyers after an attack on its East-West Pipeline last week forced it to suspend loadings from key Red Sea port of Yanbu, trade sources said. Buyers on Tuesday were bidding the price of potential alternatives such as North Sea oil higher. North Sea Forties crude jumped to a price of $136.75 a barrel, according to LSEG data, approaching the all-time high of $147.37 hit on April 13 soon after the Iran war disrupted Middle East exports. Oil [USN:L1N45703N TEXT:"futures prices"] rose by over $3 on Tuesday, with the Brent futures contract approaching $110 a barrel, on the Saudi loadings suspension and after Libya halted operations at three oil fields, heightening concerns that disruptions to supply routes could persist for weeks. The price of physical cargoes is higher than that of crude futures such as Brent in part because the physical cargoes are for delivery in a few weeks, earlier than the oil traded in futures markets. The nearby Brent futures contract is for November delivery.

item.title: SpaceX targets first Starship orbital test on September 22
item.description: SpaceX said on Tuesday it was preparing to launch its next Starship flight test as soon as September 22, a mission expected to send the vehicle into orbit for the first time and deploy Starlink V3 satellites.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SpaceX (SPCX.O) said on Tuesday it was preparing to launch its next Starship flight test as soon as September 22, a mission expected to send the vehicle into orbit for the first time and deploy Starlink V3 satellites. Starship's 14th test flight would mark a major leap in the rocket's development over its last test in July, which flew a suborbital trajectory that took the spacecraft into space before returning it to Earth without completing an orbit. The company plans to place Starship into orbit around Earth, a milestone that would allow it to test the vehicle over a longer-duration flight and deploy the first batch of Starlink V3 satellites. The mission, pending regulatory approval, is expected to last nearly 10 hours, with Starship flying about 275 km above Earth and completing about six orbits before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean west of Chile. SpaceX plans to test the booster's launch, separation, boostback and splashdown procedures, advancing the company toward its goal of a fully reusable orbital launch system.

item.title: Truist Financial to sell $5.5 billion of auto loans amid overhaul
item.description: Truist Financial said on Tuesday it has struck a deal to sell $5.5 billion of auto loans, as CEO Mike Lyons pushes to overhaul the U.S. bank and exit less profitable, non-core businesses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Truist Financial (TFC.N) said on Tuesday it has struck a deal to sell $5.5 billion of auto loans, as CEO Mike Lyons pushes to overhaul the U.S. bank and exit less profitable, non-core businesses. Here are some key details: The sale is expected to generate $5.2 billion in net proceeds for Truist and mark its exit from near-prime auto lending. The Charlotte, North Carolina-based bank also said a broad strategic review was ongoing. "There's a lot of urgency and intensity that's been added to this evaluation that really started earlier this year," Truist finance chief Mike Maguire said at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference on Tuesday. During the second quarter, Truist discontinued marine and recreational vehicle loans and reduced originations in several other less profitable consumer lending units, such as prime and non-prime auto. "In addition to implementing a more robust deposit gathering strategy, we also believe further divestitures are likely as Lyons repositions TFC for stronger growth and profitability over the next three years," RBC analyst Gerard Cassidy said. Truist said it is pairing the transaction, which is expected to close this year, with a repositioning of its securities portfolio to offset the capital created from the loan sale.

item.title: Attorney General Blanche says DOJ would probe AI-related violations
item.description: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday told reporters the Department of Justice would investigate "anybody associated" with AI if they violated the law.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche on Tuesday told reporters the Department of Justice would investigate "anybody associated" with AI if they violated the law. "As far as AI is concerned, there's a lot of criminal laws," Blanche told reporters at the White House. "So if anybody associated with AI violates criminal law, we'll investigate that." Blanche added that he did not believe the role of the Justice Department was to regulate AI.

item.title: Legislador republicano de EEUU presenta moción para destituir al jefe del Pentágono por Irán
item.description: El legislador republicano Thomas Massie presentó el martes una moción de destitución contra el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, al que acusa de abusar de su cargo al ejecutar una orden de atacar Irán sin la aprobación del Congreso.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: El legislador republicano Thomas Massie presentó el martes una moción de destitución contra el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, al que acusa de abusar de su cargo al ejecutar una orden de atacar Irán sin la aprobación del Congreso. Es poco probable que se apruebe la resolución, pero la maniobra del republicano de Kentucky podría forzar una votación en la Cámara que resultaría complicada para algunos de sus compañeros republicanos, que se preparan para abandonar Washington antes de las elecciones legislativas de noviembre. "Todo el Departamento está unido en torno a la visión del secretario y seguirá trabajando para anteponer a nuestros combatientes y a Estados Unidos", dijo el secretario de prensa del Pentágono, Kingsley Wilson, en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico. Massie presentó los artículos de destitución contra Hegseth como "privilegiados", lo que significa que la Cámara debe tramitarlos en un plazo de dos días legislativos. Massie, un crítico acérrimo de la guerra contra Irán y de la ayuda a Israel, no se presenta a la reelección. Las encuestas muestran que la guerra, que comenzó con los ataques del 28 de febrero contra Irán por parte de las fuerzas estadounidenses e israelíes, es impopular entre los votantes. Miembros del Congreso, principalmente demócratas, han votado en repetidas ocasiones a favor de resoluciones que instan a Trump a poner fin al conflicto a menos que obtenga el apoyo del Congreso, pero estas no han dado lugar a un cese de las hostilidades. Las encuestas de opinión indican que los republicanos de Trump se enfrentan a una ardua lucha para mantener el control de la Cámara de Representantes y el Senado cuando los votantes acudan a las urnas el 3 de noviembre. Los resultados de una encuesta de Reuters/Ipsos publicados el lunes mostraron que los demócratas aventajan a los republicanos por un 44% frente a un 37% en cuanto a preferencias de voto para el Congreso. La popularidad de Trump ha caído desde que comenzó la guerra, que ha interrumpido los envíos de petróleo y ha elevado los precios del combustible a casi récords, lo que ha afectado a la economía de los hogares estadounidenses.

item.title: LA28 could generate up to $40.6 billion for region, study says
item.description: The 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games could generate as much as $40.6 billion in economic output and support up to 224,000 jobs across the Greater Los Angeles region, according to a study released on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games could generate as much as $40.6 billion in economic output and support up to 224,000 jobs across the Greater Los Angeles region, according to a study released on Tuesday. The analysis by the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation, commissioned by LA28, estimated a range of $20.5 billion to $40.6 billion in economic activity during the years of preparation for the Games and through their conclusion in 2028. "The scale and breadth of the economic activity associated with the 2028 Games is significant, even when viewed through a conservative lens," said Stephen Cheung, President & CEO of LAEDC. "Our analysis shows the impact reaching across the regional economy, from jobs and labor income to local businesses, visitor spending, and long-term investment. Importantly, these findings reflect a range of potential outcomes, providing a transparent picture of the economic benefits the Games could generate for Greater Los Angeles." The estimates cover Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino and Ventura counties, and include spending on Games operations, transportation and security, capital projects, visitor activity and expenditures by independently funded organizations involved in staging the event. Games-related infrastructure investment, including transportation, airport, mobility, accessibility and venue upgrades, would be the largest source of economic impact, the report said. It estimated that about $8.35 billion in such investment has been accelerated or undertaken in connection with the event. NO-BUILD GAMES LA28 has promoted a "no-build" strategy that relies largely on existing venues and temporary facilities, rather than construction of new permanent Olympic sites. The study projected that the Games could bring about 2 million visitors to the region. Direct spending by non-resident visitors in Los Angeles County was estimated at between $1.6 billion and $4.3 billion, potentially benefiting hotels, restaurants, retailers and entertainment businesses. The report also forecast $5.1 billion to $5.9 billion in combined federal, state and local tax revenue associated with Games-related economic activity. The job estimates include positions in construction, transportation, hospitality, accommodation, security and administrative services, among other industries. LA28 said it aims to direct 75% of its addressable procurement spending to Greater Los Angeles businesses, with 25% targeted toward local and small businesses. The LAEDC said it used two methodologies to develop the estimates: a more conservative framework focused on new outside spending entering the region, and an IMPLAN input-output model that measures broader gross economic activity. Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics for the third time, after 1932 and 1984, and the Paralympic Games for the first time.

item.title: Gobierno de Trump planea una venta de munición a Israel por 2.800 millones de dólares, según fuentes
item.description: El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump tiene previsto vender a Israel un paquete de municiones por valor de 2.800 millones de dólares, que incluirá decenas de miles de bombas de 2.000 libras de gran poder destructivo, según un funcionario estadounidense al corriente de la operación.
item.dc:creator: Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump tiene previsto vender a Israel un paquete de municiones por valor de 2.800 millones de dólares, que incluirá decenas de miles de bombas de 2.000 libras de gran poder destructivo, según un funcionario estadounidense al corriente de la operación. La venta prevista, que se ha comunicado de manera informal a las comisiones pertinentes del Congreso —encargadas de evaluar las grandes ventas de armas—, incluye 20.000 MK 84 y 20.000 BLU-117, dijo el funcionario, que habló bajo condición de anonimato. La noticia sobre este paquete la publicó por primera vez el Washington Post. El Departamento de Estado y la embajada israelí no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. El apoyo de la opinión pública estadounidense a Israel ha disminuido desde que comenzó la guerra de Gaza en 2023, especialmente entre los demócratas. Una encuesta de la Universidad de Quinnipiac realizada en junio reveló que el 48% de los votantes y el 66% de los demócratas consideran que Estados Unidos apoya demasiado a Israel, lo que supone un aumento respecto al 16% y el 20% de cuando se planteó la pregunta por primera vez en 2017. Israel ha usado habitualmente bombas de 2.000 libras tanto en Gaza como en el Líbano, lo que ha suscitado el escrutinio de los expertos en derechos humanos. Según las autoridades sanitarias de Gaza, más de 73.000 palestinos han perdido la vida en la campaña militar de Israel. Una investigación de la ONU determinó que Israel había cometido genocidio en Gaza, una acusación que Tel Aviv rechaza. Israel califica sus acciones de legítima defensa, después de que militantes liderados por Hamás mataron a 1.200 personas y tomaron más de 250 rehenes en un ataque perpetrado en octubre de 2023. Estados Unidos e Israel atacaron Irán el 28 de febrero. Irán respondió con sus propios ataques contra Israel y los Estados del golfo Pérsico que albergan bases estadounidenses. Los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán y los ataques israelíes en el Líbano han causado miles de muertos y han desplazado a millones de personas.

item.title: Costo de guerra en Irán alcanza 38.000 millones de dólares: oficina presupuesto del Congreso
item.description: La guerra de Estados Unidos contra Irán ha costado hasta ahora 38.000 millones de dólares y se prevé que esa cifra aumente en 3.000 millones de dólares al mes, informó el martes el ente contable no partidista del Congreso.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: La guerra de Estados Unidos contra Irán ha costado hasta ahora 38.000 millones de dólares y se prevé que esa cifra aumente en 3.000 millones de dólares al mes, informó el martes el ente contable no partidista del Congreso. Se prevé que la guerra aumente la inflación en un 0,5% durante los tres primeros meses de 2027, según los cálculos de la Oficina Presupuestaria del Congreso, que ha contabilizado los gastos hasta el 1 de agosto. Los crecientes costos han mermado las reservas de municiones de Estados Unidos y han disparado los precios de la energía, suscitando preocupación sobre la capacidad del país para responder a otros posibles conflictos. También ha añadido presión a un presupuesto federal ya de por sí ajustado. El costo se acercaba a los 37.500 millones de dólares que el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, comunicó en una audiencia del Senado el 21 de julio. La Oficina Presupuestaria señaló que la mayor parte de los costos se debe al rápido agotamiento de las municiones, y estimó que podría llevar cinco años reponer las reservas estadounidenses. Reuters informó en agosto que Estados Unidos había utilizado "prácticamente todos" sus misiles de precisión de largo alcance durante la guerra. El Departamento de Defensa no cooperó con los auditores financieros del Congreso, según informó la CBO. Los representantes de la Casa Blanca y del Departamento de Defensa no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. El informe no incluía los costos de los recientes ataques contra buques mercantes en el estrecho de Ormuz ni las incursiones instalaciones militares estadounidenses en la región. Tampoco tenía en cuenta los gastos de endeudamiento asociados a la financiación de la guerra, que podrían sumar decenas de miles de millones de dólares al costo total.

item.title: Al Taawoun hit with stadium closure and fine over 'Jota' chants
item.description: The Saudi Arabian Football Federation’s Disciplinary and Ethics Committee on Tuesday ordered Al Taawoun to play their next two home Saudi Pro League matches behind closed doors and fined the club 100,000 riyals ($26,660) after supporters chanted the name of the late Portugal forward Diogo Jota during Saturday's match against Al Hilal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Saudi Arabian Football Federation’s Disciplinary and Ethics Committee on Tuesday ordered Al Taawoun to play their next two home Saudi Pro League matches behind closed doors and fined the club 100,000 riyals ($26,660) after supporters chanted the name of the late Portugal forward Diogo Jota during Saturday's match against Al Hilal. The sanctions stem from an incident involving Al Hilal midfielder Ruben Neves, a close friend and former teammate of Jota, who died in a car crash in Spain last year alongside his brother Andre Silva. Neves was among the pallbearers at Jota's funeral. Videos circulated on social media appeared to show sections of the crowd chanting "Jota" during Al Hilal's 6-0 win over Al Taawoun. Neves reacted by pointing to his eye and then toward the sky before saying after the match: "I hope they don't go to pray afterwards." The chants sparked widespread criticism, including from Al Nassr captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who urged authorities to take strong action. Al Hilal said it had filed a complaint with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation, describing the chants as offensive and unacceptable, while Al Taawoun condemned the behaviour and said it did not represent the club or its supporters.

item.title: Safras francesas de milho e beterraba devem ser as menores desde a década de 1970
item.description: A França deve registrar suas menores safras de milho e beterraba sacarina desde a década de 1970, depois que ondas de calor e secas prejudicaram as plantações no maior produtor agrícola da União Europeia, informou o Ministério da Agricultura do país em um relatório divulgado nesta terça-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A França deve registrar suas menores safras de milho e beterraba sacarina desde a década de 1970, depois que ondas de calor e secas prejudicaram as plantações no maior produtor agrícola da União Europeia, informou o Ministério da Agricultura do país em um relatório divulgado nesta terça-feira. Para o milho, o ministério reduziu sua previsão para a safra deste ano para 8,1 milhões de toneladas métricas, ante os 9,0 milhões inicialmente previstos no mês passado, o que representa uma queda de quase 42% em relação a 2025. Para a beterraba sacarina, sua primeira projeção de produção para 2026 ficou em 25,4 milhões de toneladas, uma queda de 29% em relação ao ano anterior. As previsões para ambas as culturas foram as mais baixas nos registros do ministério, que remontam a 1980. Dados históricos da França divulgados pela Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura (FAO) mostraram que a safra de milho seria a menor desde 1976 e a de beterraba, desde 1978. Analistas e produtores têm previsto amplamente uma queda acentuada na produção de milho e beterraba, com muitos projetando uma produção de milho abaixo de 7 milhões de toneladas. O ministério reduziu suas estimativas para a safra de trigo "soft" de 31,9 milhões para 31,7 milhões de toneladas, o que representa agora uma queda de 5% em relação ao ano anterior, e para a safra de cevada de 11,0 milhões para 10,8 milhões de toneladas, 9% abaixo do nível de 2025. (Reportagem de Gus Trompiz)

item.title: Trump taps acting EEOC general counsel Eschbach to serve permanently
item.description: President Donald Trump has nominated Catherine Eschbach, a former Morgan, Lewis & Bockius partner currently serving as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's acting general counsel, to fill that role at the anti-discrimination agency for a full term.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump has nominated Catherine Eschbach, a former Morgan, Lewis & Bockius partner currently serving as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's acting general counsel, to fill that role at the anti-discrimination agency for a full term. The White House said late Monday it had sent a slate of nominations to the Senate for confirmation that includes Eschbach, who as general counsel would continue to manage hundreds of attorneys who investigate worker complaints, broker settlements, and sue employers for discrimination. Eschbach worked at Morgan Lewis for about six years before joining the Trump administration and [USN:L1N3UB0J5 TEXT:"has represented SpaceX"], Amazon.com, Comcast and Walgreens in [USN:L1N3KS0NG TEXT:"challenges to government enforcement actions"]. She was appointed to the EEOC as its principal deputy general counsel last year after serving briefly as the director of the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs, which enforces anti-discrimination provisions in federal contracts. Eschbach oversaw the office after Trump [USN:L3N3OI09U TEXT:"wiped out an executive order from the 1960s"] that had required federal contractors to take affirmative action to address workplace discrimination, and which had been at the core of [USN:L1N40S0IR TEXT:"the office's enforcement efforts"] for decades. Eschbach has also aided inter-agency efforts to eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion programs, according to the EEOC . Trump has been critical of DEI and moved to eradicate it from not only the government but also the private sector, education, healthcare and other areas. EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, a Trump appointee, has moved [USN:L1N42D0JI TEXT:"to curtail workplace diversity programs"] including by launching a probe of DEI policies at major law firms and warning employers that many common workplace policies may be unlawful. Trump last year nominated M. Carter Crow , a partner and the global head of labor and employment at Norton Rose Fulbright, for EEOC general counsel but withdrew the pick in April. The White House did not give a reason at the time. item.title: US agency orders Tesla to answer questions on Cybercab certification
item.description: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday said Tesla must answer a series of questions by September 30 on whether it properly self-certified its autonomous Cybercab robotaxi as part of the government's investigation.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on Tuesday said Tesla (TSLA.O) must answer a series of questions by September 30 on whether it properly self-certified its autonomous Cybercab robotaxi as part of the government's investigation. NHTSA said Tesla must answer whether temporarily installed human driver controls or other equipment was part of Tesla’s basis for certifying compliance, and other questions. The auto safety regulator said this month it was examining the process and technical data the EV maker relied on to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards before deploying the robotaxi. Tesla and other robotaxi companies including Google's Waymo have backed plans by President Donald Trump's administration to change regulations so that such vehicles do not need to have steering wheels, brake pedals, rear-view mirrors or other equipment required by human drivers. Critics of robotaxis oppose the changes, saying the rules should not be waived until the companies prove that autonomous vehicles are safe. NHTSA asked Tesla to confirm whether the Cybercab robotaxis are capable of being driven by a human driver and if there are any controls in the vehicle touchscreen by which occupants can move the vehicle. It also wants Tesla to answer questions including maximum speed, geographical or time-of-day limits and other restrictions on the robotaxis. On September 3, Tesla began [USN:L6N44V1CY TEXT:"commercial deployment"] of a small number of the two-seater Cybercabs in Austin, Texas, and said it planned to gradually expand the service to additional vehicles and locations. NHTSA said the Cybercab lacks conventional manual controls, including a steering wheel, brake pedal, accelerator pedal and mirrors. In June, the agency proposed to end a government requirement for manual brake pedals in self-driving vehicles, a move that would make it easier to deploy such vehicles without human controls on U.S. roads. The agency has proposed other changes to federal safety standards to allow autonomous vehicles to avoid needing additional human driver equipment, but existing standards remain in force until those are finalized, NHTSA said. Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Under existing law, fully self-driving vehicles do not need NHTSA approval if they have steering wheels, brake pedals, mirrors and other features of human-controlled vehicles. NHTSA has authority to grant petitions to allow up to 2,500 vehicles per manufacturer yearly to operate on U.S. roads without required human controls. In July, NHTSA approved a petition for Amazon's (AMZN.O) Zoox unit for limited commercial deployment of its novel steering-wheel-free robotaxis, a first for the autonomous ride industry.

item.title: Angola delivers another big rate cut as inflation falls to single digits
item.description: Angola's central bank cut its key lending rate by 100 basis points (bps) on Tuesday, its third reduction in a row after inflation fell to single digits for the first time in more than a decade.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Gomes
item.content:encoded: Angola's central bank cut its key lending rate by 100 basis points (bps) on Tuesday, its third reduction in a row after inflation fell to single digits for the first time in more than a decade. The Bank of Angola lowered its policy rate (AOINTR=ECI) to 14.75% from 15.75%, following cuts of [USN:L8N43G1J4 TEXT:"125 bps"] in July and [USN:L8N41R1NA TEXT:"50 bps"] in May. Inflation in the Southern African oil producer eased to 8.78% year-on-year (AOCPIY=ECI) in August from 9.33% in July. It was last in single digits in 2015. The central bank maintained its year-end inflation forecast at 8.6% but sharply raised this year's economic growth forecast to 6.15% from a projection of 3.6% in July, citing a stronger performance in both oil and non-oil sectors. Angola's economy has benefited from high global energy prices linked to the Iran war . The International Monetary Fund [USN:L8N4510C2 TEXT:"has urged"] policymakers to channel oil revenue windfalls into debt reduction and building fiscal buffers. Finance Minister Vera Daves de Sousa told Reuters last week the government was likely to [USN:L8N4510C2 TEXT:"raise its 2027 oil price assumption"] from the $61 per barrel in this year's budget, though it would retain a conservative forecasting approach. Liandra da Silva, a Nedbank economist, said while Angola's status as an oil exporter offered some protection from external shocks, persistent increases in shipping costs and imported input prices could still drive some imported inflationary pressures.

item.title: Texas Republican's post on Asian Americans at UT Austin sparks accusations of racism
item.description: A Republican nominee for a Texas office drew bipartisan criticism after posting a photo from a University of Texas football game that critics called racist, portraying the Austin campus as dominated by foreign students contrary to enrollment data.
item.dc:creator: David Hood-Nuño
item.content:encoded: A Republican nominee for a Texas office drew bipartisan criticism after posting a photo from a University of Texas football game that critics called racist, portraying the Austin campus as dominated by foreign students contrary to enrollment data. Bo French, the Republican nominee for Texas railroad commissioner, drew a sharp rebuke from fellow Republicans as well as Democrats after posting a crowd shot at a University of Texas football game, while suggesting that what appeared to be students of South Asian descent reflected a large foreign-born or international student presence on campus. "I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined," French posted to his X account. He went on to claim that UT prioritizes foreign students in admissions and feared Texans were losing opportunities at the university. "I weep for the families in Texas who can’t get into UT because they prioritize foreigners over Texans," he said. I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined. pic.twitter.com/Ys1bql0y4U — Bo French (@bofrench) September 13, 2026 But enrollment figures released by the University of Texas at Austin show international students account for less than 10% of the total student body. Total enrollment reached 55,000 students for the fall 2025 semester, including 5,140 international students. Texas residents make up 80.5% of all enrolled students. For the undergraduate class, international students make up 4.3%, and a state law requires 90% of every incoming freshman class to be Texas residents. UT Austin automatically admits the top 5% of performers — who are also Texas residents — at every high school in the state. The Texas legislature designed the initiative to promote diversity without explicitly considering race. As in most of the country, Texas high school students are separated by geography, income and demographics, and by guaranteeing admission to top students at each high school, the statewide policy helps ensure universities draw from a broad cross-section of Texas communities. That means more than 90% of students at UT Austin are domestic, and more than four out of every five are Texans. Vedant Nair, 24, who graduated from UT in 2024, said his parents immigrated to Oklahoma in the 1990s from Mumbai so his father could pursue an MBA at Oklahoma State University. Nair was born in Oklahoma City and recalls running around in a child-size OSU Cowboys football helmet and driving a mini John Deere tractor. His upbringing, he said, was no different than those of his fellow Texans after his family moved to Dallas in elementary school. Attending UT Austin was a dream come true, and a normal, American experience, he said. "If you stripped away my name and skin color, I think my story is pretty similar to a lot of other Texans at massive public high schools," Nair said. "The point is that myself, and all the other kids in that picture, are just regular American kids." University spokespeople and French did not respond to a request for comment. The debate touches on a broader political argument that non-U.S. citizens are "displacing" American students at elite public universities, and the country at large. French's remarks drew criticism from political figures and other social media users, who characterized the posts as racist or xenophobic. Rodney Coates, a sociology professor at Miami University in Ohio, said French's comments echoed longstanding anti-immigrant and anti-Asian narratives in the U.S. that have historically portrayed minority groups as threats to opportunities for others. "It's easier to come up with a racist argument to organize a group of people under the presumption that, hey, they're hurting your chances," Coates said. Such appeals often have little to do with the people being targeted and instead seek to mobilize voters by portraying them as victims. "Hate is one of the easiest means of organizing," he said. University figures show white students made up about 31.5% of enrollment in 2024 to 2025, Hispanic students 25.5% and Asian students 22.4%. University reporting treats race and ethnicity separately from international student status, meaning most students categorized as Asian are U.S. citizens or permanent residents rather than international students. The image French shared was a screenshot from a video posted by the official athletics account at UT Austin. He did not include information identifying the citizenship, immigration status, residency or enrollment status of any individuals shown. For Nair, the unfortunate part of French's post was that it criticized a high point in school-pride history: the football team defeated The Ohio State University, the No. 1-ranked football team in the country. "I don't think there is anything more American than people in cowboy hats yelling their heads off after one of the greatest comeback wins in college football history," he said.

item.title: Iran war cost hits $38 billion, forecast to rise $3 billion a month, CBO says
item.description: The six-month-old U.S. war against Iran has cost $38 billion so far and that amount is projected to rise by $3 billion a month, Congress' nonpartisan bookkeeper reported on Tuesday, as the Trump administration searches for ways to end the conflict and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: The six-month-old U.S. war against Iran has cost $38 billion so far and that amount is projected to rise by $3 billion a month, Congress' nonpartisan bookkeeper reported on Tuesday, as the Trump administration searches for ways to end the conflict and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz. The war is expected to increase inflation by 0.5% in the first three months of 2027, according to the Congressional Budget Office accounting, which totaled expenses through August 1. The mounting costs have strained U.S. munitions stockpiles and driven up energy prices, raising concerns about the country's ability to respond to other potential conflicts and adding pressure on an already stretched federal budget. The cost was close to the $37.5 billion that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reported at [USN:L1N43N0ZF TEXT:"a Senate hearing on July 21."] The budget office said the majority of the costs stem from the rapid drawdown of munitions, estimating that it could take five years to replenish U.S. stockpiles. Reuters reported in August that [USN:L1N43W1IH TEXT:"the U.S. had used "virtually all""] of its long-range precision missiles during the war. The Department of Defense did not cooperate with congressional financial auditors, CBO reported. White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly described President Donald Trump's attacks on Iran as "decisive action" to prevent Tehran from harming U.S. personnel or interests. She said in a statement that the U.S. military has "more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of the Commander-in-Chief’s strategic goals and beyond.” Chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell disputed the report's findings of munitions shortages and said, "We have everything required to strike at the time and place of the president’s choosing." The cost inquiry was conducted at the request of the top Democrat on the U.S. House of Representatives Budget Committee, Brendan Boyle of Pennsylvania. “Donald Trump’s disastrous war in Iran has already taken the lives of brave American servicemembers and left others wounded," Boyle said in a statement. "Beyond that human toll, this nonpartisan CBO report makes clear that the war has also cost American taxpayers tens of billions of dollars and counting, while continuing to drive up costs." Eighteen U.S. military service members have died in the Iran war. The report did not include costs of recent strikes on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on U.S. military installations in the region. It also did not factor in the borrowing expenses associated with financing the war, which could add tens of billions of dollars to the total cost. IMPACT ON US READINESS The CBO accounting found the war could have sprawling consequences for the U.S. defense posture and the domestic economy. The deficit in critical munitions, including missile interceptors, risks hampering the Pentagon's response in the event of another major conflict, such as potential hostilities involving China and Taiwan, CBO said. At the July hearing in the Senate, Hegseth pleaded for nearly $90 billion in emergency funding to restock munitions supplies. “Without these funds, we face critical shortfalls,” Hegseth said. The Pentagon’s inspector general reported this week that Iran had damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings on U.S. bases in the Middle East as well as aircraft including fighter jets, refueling planes and drones. It put the war cost through June 19 at $33.4 billion, saying the amount included about $184 million in damages to U.S. diplomatic facilities from Iranian strikes. Energy shocks caused by attacks in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil traveled before the war — and on energy facilities in neighboring Gulf countries have sharply increased prices for consumers and global producers. The rising cost of the war also threatens to [USN:L6N44O018 TEXT:"weigh on deteriorating U.S. fiscal health"]. The nation's total public debt surpassed $40 trillion in August. Trump regularly contrasts the Iran war with the U.S. invasions of Iraq and Afghanistan that followed the September 11, 2001, attacks. The eight-year U.S. war in Iraq, which involved more than 100,000 ground troops at its peak, [USN:BRE92D0PH TEXT:"cost $2 trillion"], Reuters reported. The two-decade-long U.S. conflict in Afghanistan, which also involved more than 100,000 troops at its most intense, cost $2.3 trillion , according to Brown University's Costs of War project.

item.title: Revolut obtiene licencia bancaria en Colombia, iniciará operaciones en 2027
item.description: La fintech británica Revolut obtuvo su licencia bancaria en Colombia, operación que iniciará en 2027, dijo el martes a Reuters el presidente de la firma para el país sudamericano, Diego Caicedo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La fintech británica Revolut obtuvo su licencia bancaria en Colombia, operación que iniciará en 2027, dijo el martes a Reuters el presidente de la firma para el país sudamericano, Diego Caicedo. La licencia es la máxima que se otorga por el regulador local para las instituciones financieras, con lo que Revolut planea abarcar todos los productos bancarios con la meta de convertirse en el tercer o cuarto jugador del mercado local en los próximos cinco años, dijo el directivo. "El arranque va a ser nuestras cuentas de depósito, la cuenta Revolut, que es muy especial porque no solamente permite administrar y manejar dinero, sino que también va a tener bolsillos de ahorro de alto rendimiento", explicó Caicedo. "También venimos con múltiples tarjetas de crédito y vamos a salir con los créditos de libre inversión el próximo año". Revolut invertirá en Colombia 62 millones de dólares que se destinarán a infraestructura bancaria digital local y a tecnología financiera, monto que se suma a los 62 millones de dólares invertidos en una primera fase. "Esta autorización definitiva permitirá a Revolut operar como un banco regulado en Colombia, marcando otro paso clave hacia la transformación del panorama financiero colombiano", dijo la firma en un comunicado. Revolut cuenta con licencias bancarias en Francia, Australia y el Reino Unido, en tanto que recibió la aprobación condicional en Estados Unidos y le otorgaron una licencia de pagos en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos y en Perú. En Argentina la firma está completando la adquisición de la unidad financiera local de BNP Paribas. "Vamos a tener los principales mercados de América Latina", afirmó Caicedo. Revolut cuenta con más de 80 millones de clientes y al cierre de 2025 alcanzó ingresos de 6.000 millones de dólares, equivalentes a un incremento de 46% interanual, además de ganancias antes de impuestos de 2.300 millones de dólares.
